about.title: Wheatland Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Wheatland's small-town footprint sits alongside busy stretches of Rt 65, Spenceville Road, and Wheatland Road, where delivery drivers, utility crews, and agricultural workers move through daily. When someone gets hurt on the job here, the path forward isn't always simple. California generally requires injured workers to go through workers' compensation rather than sue their employer directly, but that's not the whole story. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to the injury, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside your comp benefits. LawProactive doesn't practice law or charge any fee; we simply connect you with an independent attorney in our network who can look at the specifics of your Wheatland workplace injury, explain your options in plain language, and help you understand whether a third-party claim applies. Every case is different, and time limits matter, so getting clarity early can make a real difference.

whyChoose.title: Why Wheatland Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding the Exclusive Remedy Rule
items.desc: California workers' comp is usually the only route against your employer, but that doesn't close the door on every claim. An attorney can help you see if a third party, like a subcontractor or another driver, may also bear responsibility.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: Reporting an injury to your employer within 30 days is required, and California law makes retaliation for doing so illegal. An independent attorney can help you understand your rights if you feel pressured after reporting.

items.title: Awareness of the Two-Year Clock
items.desc: Third-party injury claims in California carry a two-year filing deadline, separate from your workers' comp process. Missing that window can end an otherwise valid claim, so early guidance matters.

items.question: I was hurt on Wheatland Road while driving for work—does workers' comp cover that?
items.answer: Workers' comp typically covers injuries that happen while performing job duties, including driving routes on roads like Wheatland Road or SR-65. If another driver caused the crash, you may also have a separate third-party claim beyond workers' comp. An independent attorney can review the details and explain how both pieces might fit together.

items.question: What if my employer says I waited too long to report my injury?
items.answer: California generally expects injuries to be reported within 30 days, but circumstances vary and some injuries develop over time. Talking with an attorney can help clarify whether your situation still qualifies for benefits. Don't assume the door is closed without getting informed first.

items.question: Is there really no cost to use LawProactive?
items.answer: Correct, LawProactive is a free connection service, and we are not a law firm ourselves. Attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if your claim results in a recovery.
